LettertotheEditor
Therapeutic considerations in a case of progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus
Dear Editor,
Progressiveencephalomyelitiswithrigidityandmyoclonus(PERM)
isaninflammatorydisorderofthestiff-personsyndromespectrumthat
presents subacutely with trunk and limb rigidity, muscle spasms,
brainstemdysfunction,andautonomicinstability[1,2].PERMhasbeen
strongly associated with IgG1 and IgG3 autoantibodies against the
glycinereceptoralpha-1subunit(GlyRα1)[3,4].Glycinereceptorsfa-
cilitate inhibitory signaling in the brainstem and spinal cord. Auto-
antibodiesagainstGlyRα1showpathogeniccharacteristicsinvitrosuch
as complement activation and receptor internalization [4]. Further,
mutations of GlyRα1 result in hyperekplexia, a neurologic disorder
characterized by extreme hypertonia and exaggerated startle that re-
semblesthephenotypeofPERM[5].Despitepathologicabnormalities
localizable to the CNS, characteristic MRI findings have not been
identifiedinPERMwith72%ofpatientsshowingnoabnormalities.The
cerebrospinalfluid(CSF)howevershowssignsofinflammationin60%
of patients, while intrathecal synthesis of GlyRα1autoantibodies has
been demonstrated in all cases examined [4]. In many cases, im-
munotherapy leads to significant clinical improvements [4,6]. We
presentacaseofsevereGlyRα1-positivePERMwhereimmunotherapies
were applied per current protocols; however, a desirable outcomeof
independentlivingwasnotachieved.
1. Case
A 63-year-old man with chronic hearing loss (since the age of
9years)andhypertensiondevelopeddecreasedsleeprequirementsand
disorganizedbehaviorforfivemonthsfollowedbygaitdisturbanceand
myoclonus.Initialexamrevealedrightesotropia,ptosis,anisocoriaand
ataxic gait. Normal blood tests included creatinine kinase, thyroid
testing,anti-nuclearantibodiesandextractablenuclearautoantibodies.
CSFtestingshowedpleocytosis(18nucleatedcells,94%lymphocytes),
proteinof62mg/dLandglucoselevelswithinnormallimitswithne-
gative infectious workup. Electroencephalogram (EEG) showed gen-
eralizedslowingbutnoseizures.Magneticresonanceimaging(MRI)of
the brain, performed two days after lumbar puncture (LP), revealed
mild diffuse pachymeningeal enhancement, bilateral optic nerve en-
hancement and a prominent left anterior cavernous sinus (Fig. 1). A
spinalMRIshowednoevidenceofabnormalspinalcordsignalandno
evidenceofextraduralegressofCSFintheparaspinalsofttissue.
Thepatient'smentalstatusworsenedoveraweek,andhedeveloped
diffusetremor,rigidity,myoclonicjerksanddysautonomia.Herequired
intubationduetosubsegmentalpulmonaryembolism,andpropofoland
dexmedetomidine were necessary to control violent myoclonic jerks,
sympathetic storming, and agitation. Ultimately, he required tra-
cheostomyandgastrostomytube.RepeatCSFstudiesshowedpleocy-
tosis(11nucleatedcells,98%lymphocytes),normalprotein,elevated
IgGindex,andcentralnervoussystem(CNS)-specificoligoclonalbands.

performed seven days after the second LP showed stable pachyme-
ningeal and optic nerve enhancement and prominent left cavernous
sinus,inadditionbilateralthinconvexitysubduraleffusions(Fig.1).
Immunotherapywasempiricallystartedwithhighdosesteroidsand
therapeutic plasmapheresis. Despite incomplete plasmapheresis ses-
sionsduetoautonomicinstability,thepatient'sclinicalconditionsta-
bilized. He was weaned from sedation, able to intermittently follow
simplecommands,andhadreducedmyoclonus.Hereceivedrituximab
as second-line immunotherapy once GlyRα1 autoantibodies returned
positive.Twelvedaysafterhisfirstrituximabinfusion,serumandCSF
samples were again tested for GlyRα1 autoantibodies and remained
positive(atthattimepoint7nucleatedcells,100%lymphocyteswere
foundintheCSF).Hismyoclonus,rigidity,anddysautonomiaresolved.
However, he remained cognitively impaired with inattention and
minimalverbaloutput.Hesustainedalengthyhospitaladmissiondue
todifficultiesweaninghistracheostomyandwaseventuallydischarged
toaskillednursingfacility,wherehisconditionremainedstablewitha
modifiedRankinscalescoreof4sixmonthspostdischarge.Outpatient
positron emission tomography (PET) CT did not reveal fluorodeox-
yglucose-avidmalignancy.
2. Discussion
WedescribeapatientwithtypicalPERMthatpresentedfivemonths
postsymptominitiation,wherediagnosiswasmadeafterthe patient
had significantly deteriorated and had been transferred to the ICU.
Unlikemanyreportedcases,ourpatientdidnotshowmarkedresponse
to immunotherapy. Although he stabilized and was weaned from se-
dation, he continued to require continuous nursing support.
Importantly,thepatientcontinuedtoharborGlyRα1autoantibodiesin
theserumandCSFdespiteintravenoushighdosesteroids,plasmaex-
change and rituximab [4,6]. Monitoring autoantibody titers was not
possible in this case, as the cell-based assay used to detect GlyRα1
autoantibodies (Mayo Clinic Laboratories) does not currently have a
titratablecomponent.Whentreatmentoptionsarediscussed,itshould
